transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-02
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Carmen Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Oliver Grant (StrataScale Head Alliances), Priya Mehta (GTM Lead), Samir Reddy (Solutions Architect)
Shared artifacts: Drive: https://redwood.example/drive/CoSell_Playbook_v1, Draft account map: https://redwood.example/sheets/StrataScaleAccounts

Summary:
Quick partner co-sell sprint to align on 12 high-priority accounts, triage blackout/risk scenarios (procurement, NDA/po issues), and agree next steps for joint outreach and a short technical benchmark. Focus: clarify roles, timeline to pilot, and gating criteria for Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted.

Topics covered:
- Account mapping and prioritization
- Joint outbound motion and executive intro cadence
- Procurement/legal risks (NDA, SOC2, data residency)
- Technical gating: dedicated capacity vs hosted API, sandbox perf test plan
- Joint collateral and mutual close plan

Action items (recap in call):
- Maya to share draft playbook + one-pager (drive link)
- Liam to spin up sandbox and perf checklist
- Priya to push account list with contacts and current status
- Oliver to secure exec sponsor and coordinate intro

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Okay, thanks everyone for hopping on. Um, quick check — can you all see my screen? I've got the draft playbook up, if that's helpful later.
[00:12] Oliver Grant: Yep, we can see it. Thanks, Maya. Really appreciate you folks moving quickly on this.
[00:18] Priya Mehta: Hey — thanks. We, uh, prioritized a list internally, but wanted to run it by you, make sure it's aligned with your capacity and regions.
[00:27] Liam O'Connor: Cool. Before we dive account-by-account, quick frame: we aim for two tracks — target pilot accounts (fast close), and enterprise plays (longer, require Dedicated or private options). We'll flag any "blackout" scenarios — procurement or data residency blockers.
[00:41] Samir Reddy: By blackout you mean like when legal says no because of cross-border data?
[00:46] Liam O'Connor: Exactly, or when procurement requires on-prem or very specific KMS/HSM patterns that we haven't scoped.
[00:52] Carmen Ruiz: And from a success perspective, we want a clear canary — one pilot that proves both GTM and technical fit within 3–6 weeks.
[01:03] Maya Patel: Great. Priya — could you walk us through your top 12? If you call out two pilots we can map Redwood playbook to each.
[01:10] Priya Mehta: Yep — so top 12, the first four are mid-market cloud-native, quick procurement. Next three are regulated (health/finance) — may need SOC2 plus VPC. Remaining five are long-cycle accounts with heavy platforms procurement. The first pilot we suggest is 'AetnaData' — they want an assistant proof for claims triage, should be a good fit.
[01:34] Oliver Grant: Small correction — it's actually 'AetnaDatalake' — sometimes the names get munged in sheets.
[01:40] Maya Patel: (laughs) totally, spreadsheet names always a struggle. For AetnaDatalake, Samir — what would be the gating tech requirements?
[01:49] Samir Reddy: They need encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, and per-country data residency rules. Also a SOC2 attestation is a must.
[01:57] Liam O'Connor: We can support CMK via KMS integrations on Redwood Private, and we have SOC2 docs — will share. Note, for per-country residency we usually recommend Private/VPC deployment; hosted may not guarantee that.
[02:09] Priya Mehta: That makes sense. So that would push AetnaDatalake into the "private" track. Is timeline for that significantly longer?
[02:17] Liam O'Connor: Yes, private deployment has more lead time — network setup, KMS validation, and we do an ops checklist. Typically 6–12 weeks depending on onboarding windows. Hosted pilot could be 1–2 weeks.
[02:29] Maya Patel: Ok — so maybe pick one pilot for hosted fast win, one for private to prove compliance. Priya, do you have one account that fits hosted?
[02:37] Priya Mehta: Yup — 'TilePoint' fits hosted, they are cloud native, small procurement, willing to sign a time-limited DPA.
[02:44] Oliver Grant: TilePoint also has a champion in product; likely to run a 6-week evaluation and then expand.
[02:49] Carmen Ruiz: Good. We'll aim to operationalize — Redwood will do the sandbox perf, joint one-pager, and StrataScale will do the intro and champion enablement.
[02:58] Samir Reddy: Quick technical question — for the sandbox perf, what's the typical config you test? GPUs? batch sizes?
[03:04] Liam O'Connor: For these pilots we'll usually mirror the expected production footprint — a mid-sized T4 or A10x GPU for generation workloads, run 200–500 requests to surface latency/throughput, and test prefix caching behavior. We'll send a perf checklist.
[03:17] Priya Mehta: Any chance you can also validate cost per 1k tokens estimate? Our finance team asks for ballpark.
[03:23] Maya Patel: Yep, we'll provide an estimate range; we'll call out tradeoffs — lower latency increases cost, dedicated is more predictable per-token but requires commitment.
[03:32] Priya Mehta: About the commitment — if a customer picks Dedicated, do we have a quick canary path? Like start hosted then handoff to Dedicated?
[03:39] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we support lift-and-shift with pinned model versions. There's an onboarding window for reserved capacity, but we can set a canary policy to serve from hosted until dedicated is warmed up then switch.
[03:50] (brief crosstalk)
[03:54] Oliver Grant: On procurement — we've seen delays when legal wants a modified DPA. Is Redwood flexible on contract language?
[04:01] Maya Patel: We have standard terms, and our legal team will review modifications on enterprise deals. For big customers we expect some negotiation, but we try to limit RTO clauses that block pilots.
[04:11] Priya Mehta: Good. If legal asks for change log or audit trail — do you provide audit logs and request tracing?
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: Yes, audit logs are available in Redwood Console for Private and Dedicated, and hosted has request-level logs for a retention period. We can narrow retention for enterprise or enable longer retention as an add-on.
[04:29] Priya Mehta: Perfect. That helps.
[04:33] Maya Patel: Let's go account-by-account quickly — I'll call the sheet row and we'll assign track and owner.
[04:38] Maya Patel: Row 1 TilePoint — hosted pilot — owner: Priya + Maya.
[04:45] Priya Mehta: Confirmed.
[04:47] Maya Patel: Row 2 AetnaDatalake — private track — owner: Oliver + Liam.
[04:54] Oliver Grant: Yep. We'll need a legal touchpoint early.
[04:58] Maya Patel: Row 3 Mercury Bank — high risk, long procurement, regulated — recommend engage sales + Redwood legal early.
[05:07] Samir Reddy: For Mercury Bank they need static model weights — is that a problem?
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: Could you clarify static model weights — do you mean you want to ensure weights don't change and to host model artifacts on-prem?
[05:18] Samir Reddy: Yeah, they prefer model artifacts not to be updated without explicit approvers.
[05:23] Liam O'Connor: We have version pinning and model registry controls; on Private we can keep a specific model binary in their environment. On Hosted, we have version pins but binaries remain on Redwood.
[05:33] Carmen Ruiz: That maps to the enterprise play and longer ramp. We'll add legal and security owners.
[05:38] Priya Mehta: A couple of asks from our sales ops: do you have a partner co-sell checklist that we can reuse?
[05:45] Maya Patel: Yes — that's essentially the playbook we're sharing. It has sections: roles & responsibilities, cadence template, joint outreach email templates, pilot success metrics (time-to-value, accuracy thresholds), and escalation paths.
[05:56] Oliver Grant: If possible, can we include a short 'no-go' checklist so our reps don't waste cycles on accounts likely blocked by residency?
[06:03] Liam O'Connor: We'll add a blocklist — residency, mandatory on-prem, or hsm-only KMS are typical no-go items for hosted.
[06:12] Priya Mehta: On collateral — can we get a one-page for the field that says: "What Redwood solves for partners" — low-lift pilot + clear compliance play?
[06:21] Maya Patel: Absolutely — one-pager on the way.
[06:24] (pause, notes)
[06:29] Samir Reddy: A small technical red flag — some of our accounts use old TLS stacks and FIPS requirements. How strictly do you enforce ciphers?
[06:36] Liam O'Connor: On Private we can match cipher requirements. Hosted we follow modern TLS, and we can support FIPS endpoints on Dedicated with some configuration. We'll capture this in the tech gating doc.
[06:48] Priya Mehta: Great. Regarding executive intro — Oliver, who is the sponsor on your side?
[06:53] Oliver Grant: I'm working to lock in Maria Jensen at StrataScale exec; she wants a 20-minute exec brief next week.
[06:59] Maya Patel: Perfect — we'll prep an executive brief and tailored one-pager for Maria.
[07:03] Carmen Ruiz: For timelines, let's align on these milestones: playbook v1 by 2026-05-06, pilot kickoff (TilePoint) by 2026-05-18, private onboarding prep kickoff by 2026-05-20.
[07:14] Priya Mehta: Those look okay to me.
[07:17] Maya Patel: And for the perf sandbox — Liam, you'll send checklist + account invite?
[07:22] Liam O'Connor: Yes — I'll spin up the sandbox, capture expected QPS and token size, and send invites to Samir and his team by 2026-05-08.
[07:31] (typing/background noise)
[07:35] Oliver Grant: Quick FYI — we've had competitors ping some accounts. Anthropic has been active with one regional bank and Databricks surfaced as a platform partner in a separate account. We should call out overlapping sellers.
[07:46] Maya Patel: Good to know — we'll add competitor tags in the account map.
[07:50] Priya Mehta: One last question on revenue split and attribution in co-sell motions — do you have a recommended model for partners?
[07:58] Carmen Ruiz: From the CS side, we usually recommend a simple crediting model — partner brings customer, Redwood invoices, then we have a partner commission or rebate. But for larger deals we can set bespoke arrangements.
[08:10] Priya Mehta: That helps.
[08:13] Maya Patel: Okay, we'll wrap with explicit next steps. Oliver, can you confirm Maria intro by EOD Friday (2026-05-08)?
[08:21] Oliver Grant: I'll chase and update the sheet.
[08:23] Maya Patel: Great — Maya to share playbook by 2026-05-06, Liam to share sandbox invite by 2026-05-08, Priya to share account map by 2026-05-07.
[08:34] (end-of-meeting recap)

Note on transcription: occasional speaker labels may be approximate; system did a best-effort transcription.

End of transcript.
